title: PYCT 5: Error Spotting - 5

questions.question:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Three more elevated roads have been propose in the new plan to unclog the traffic in Delhi.

options.text: to unclog the traffic in Delhi

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **have been propose**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in passive voice. In passive voice, the verb should be in the third form.
 
• Therefore, change 'have been propose' to 'have been **proposed'.**

questions.question:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Tilak rowed through the river and tied his boat on the other side.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. **through the river**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct phrase will be across the river.
 
• Whenever we travel by dividing into two-part we use **across**.

questions.question:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The Cannes Film Festival attract some of the world's most famous people.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. attract some of.**

 
• In the given sentence the verb **'attract**' has been used which is wrong here.
 
• In the given sentence the **subject is singular** i.e. film festival, hence, a **singular verb** i.e. **attracts** will be used.
 
• So, the correct sentence will be: **The Cannes Film Festival attracts some of the world's most famous people.**

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Different-coloured natural foods not only put a smile on children's faces and also beneﬁt their overall growth.

options.text: put a smile on children's faces

questions.solution:
• The correct answer is **Option 2).**
 
• There is a rule that the** **conjunction** 'Not only' **is always followed by** 'but also'.**
 
• **Therefore, the correct sentence is** *'Different-coloured natural foods not only put a smile on children's faces but also beneﬁt their overall growth.'*

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Even Sharat tried his best, he could not clear all the examination papers in one attempt.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Even Sharat tried his best.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• As we have two sentences here we need a **conjunction** to connect both these sentence.
 
• **Even **is an **adverb** we have to replace it with a conjunction to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• As one sentence is positive and another is negative, so we need to use contradictory conjunction.
 
• **Although **is one such type of conjunction and will make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• We can also use '**Even though**'. 

**The correct sentence will be **- ***Although** Sharat tried his best, he could not clear all the examination papers in one attempt. OR** Even though** Sharat tried his best, he could not clear all the examination papers in one attempt.*

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Deepak said that he would pack few things he had and vacate the hostel room the next day.

options.text: Deepak said that he would pack

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **pack few things he had.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• We need to change **few** with **the few** for making the sentence correct.
 
• Few means almost nothing and has a negative sense.
 
• But since there is something definite in the room to vacate, we need to use either **'the few'. **
 
• **'The few' **means not many but all. 
 
 
• **Ex. The few** words that she spoke are deeply ingrained in my head.
 
 

**The correct sentence will be - ***Deepak said that he would pack **the **few things he had and vacate the hostel room the next day.*

questions.question:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. 

The Public Works Department has propose to construct an elevated corridor which will run parallel to the National highway.

options.text: The Public Works Department has propose

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. The Public Works Department has proposed.**

 
• The given sentence is in **present perfect tense** and in present perfect tense** third form of verb** is used.
 
• Hence, **'proposed'** will be used in place of 'propose'.
 
• So, the correct sentence will be: **The Public Works Department has proposed to construct an elevated corridor which will run parallel to the National highway.**

questions.question:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Billionaire Philip is the owner of the luxury yacht Lionheart, which worth an estimated $150 million.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 3.**
 
• The verb 'is' is missing after 'which'. 
 
• **Therefore, the correct sentence is** 'Billionaire Philip is the owner of the luxury yacht Lionheart, which **is **worth an estimated $150 million'.

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

Mrs. Sangeeta Malik is one of the favourite teacher of most children in our school.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. one of the favourite teacher.**

 
• A **plural** noun is used after** 'one of the'.**
 
• Hence, **'teachers'** will be used in the given sentence.

So, the correct sentence will be:** Mrs. Sangeeta Malik is one of the favourite teachers of most children in our school.**

**Note: Most** can be used as a** determiner, **in general**,** to refer to **a quantity of an unspecific group of people or things.**

**E.g. Most** students ask questions.

There is no need for placing article '**the'** in this situation. So there is no error in the last part of the sentence.

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

The launch of the small electric car will depend to the willingness of buyers to pay more for it.

options.text: of buyers to pay more for it

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 3.**
 
• The error lies in the wrong usage of the preposition 'to' which is used to determine the movement. 'to' should be replaced by **'on' which indicates the state of something. The verb 'depend' takes the preposition 'on'.**
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence is 'The launch of the small electric car will depend **on** the willingness of buyers to pay more for it.'
